name: Simple wooden push-toy car (Ana White plan as published by The Project Lady): pine body, dowel axles, slab wheels

sources.what: typical 1-1/2in x 1/2in slab wheel with 1/4in hole
SDFWA toy-making reference: 9/32in hole for a rotating 1/4in dowel axle; 7/32in axle-peg tenon glues into 15/64in

overallDimsMm.note: x=length, y=width across wheels: 2-1/2in (63.5mm) dowel + ~1/2in wheels => ~76mm estimated if wheels sit flush on dowel ends; body outline is a template whose dims are not in the page text

parts.name: body
parts.material: select pine board, 4in wide x 3/4in thick
parts.notes: profile traced from template; length not stated. Body lies flat: its 3/4in thickness is across the car, between the wheels.

parts.name: wheel
parts.notes: 1-1/4in to 1-1/2in dia with 1/4in center hole; 1/2in thickness from typical supplier

joins.notes: one wheel glued to each dowel first; the second wheel glued after the dowel passes through the body
dowel spins in a body hole drilled slightly larger than 1/4in (SDFWA uses 9/32in = 7.14mm)

assembly.stepsSource: approximate count of primary steps on The Project Lady page (template, cut, round/sand, drill, paint, wheel sub-assemblies, final wheel attach)
order: glue one wheel on each dowel
pass dowel through body, glue second wheel

confidence: medium: wheel dia, dowel dia/length, glue-wheel-to-spinning-axle method and 4in x 3/4in stock are quoted from the page; body length/height and axle hole positions NOT available (template only); step count is approximate; 9/32in clearance hole is from SDFWA, not this plan.
notes: Classic pattern: rotating dowel axle in an oversized body bore, wheels glued to axle. The common alternative is a fixed axle peg (7/32in tenon) glued into the body with the wheel spinning on the peg.
